title: Check yourself: Plugins, dependencies, sharing and the practice

questions.stem: A plugin declares a dependency on `~2.1.0`, and the dependency's maintainer publishes 2.1.4 and then 2.2.0. Which version do the plugin's users receive?

options.text: 2.2.0, because a range always follows the newest release that exists
options.says: Ruled out because a pinned range does not follow the newest release: "Without a version constraint, a dependency moves to each new release its marketplace publishes".

options.text: 2.1.0, because a range freezes the first version that it matched once
options.says: Ruled out because the dependency "installs at the highest git tag that satisfies this range", which is 2.1.4 and not the first match.

options.text: Neither, because ranges are resolved only for plugins that carry no version
options.says: Ruled out because "resolution is by git tag" for a git-backed dependency, and the object form with a `version` range is how a dependency is constrained.

options.text: 2.1.4, because the range takes patch updates and not the 2.2 line
options.says: The page says with `~2.1.0` "users who have your plugin installed keep receiving `2.1.x` patches of the dependency and never move to `2.2`."

questions.stem: A team wants contributors to get a plugin when they open the repository, with no manual install step. Where does the configuration go?

options.says: Ruled out because the manifest is "called the manifest, that names the plugin", so it describes the plugin and does not reach contributors who have not installed it.

options.text: The project's `.claude/settings.json`, under two named keys
options.says: The page says to "set two keys in the repository's `.claude/settings.json`", so that the marketplace and the enabled plugin reach every contributor.

options.text: The `marketplace.json` catalog, in the entry for that bundle
options.says: Ruled out because the catalog is only where plugins are listed, and the page has the repository name it: "Add the marketplace under `extraKnownMarketplaces`, keyed by the marketplace's own `name`".

options.text: Each person's launch command, using the `--plugin-dir` flag
options.says: Ruled out because `--plugin-dir` "loads a plugin for one session without installing it", so it is neither shared nor lasting.

questions.stem: An agent file shipped inside a plugin sets `permissionMode: bypassPermissions` to run quietly. What happens?

options.text: The value is dropped at load time, because the loader skips such fields
options.says: The page says "These fields are ignored when loading agents from a plugin."

options.text: The plugin fails to load, because the loader rejects the whole file
options.says: Ruled out because "These fields are ignored when loading agents from a plugin", so the file still loads.

options.text: The agent skips every prompt, exactly as the value says it should
options.says: Ruled out because the fields are "ignored when loading agents from a plugin", so the agent keeps its normal prompts.

options.text: The agent runs quietly, but only in a folder that the person has trusted
options.says: Ruled out because the fields are "ignored" whatever the folder, and trust only decides whether `extraKnownMarketplaces` applies. The page names the fix: "Ship the guard in `hooks/hooks.json`."
